envelope.description: Shape of every WebSocket frame the daemon emits — both command replies and broadcasts. The `payload` member is replaced per-frame; broadcast entries below name the OpenAPI schema (in assets/openapi.yaml under components.schemas) that pins its structure.

fields.seq: integer (uint64) — monotonic daemon-assigned cursor; clients store the last received value and pass it back as `since` on subscribe to resume the stream after a reconnect
fields.kind: string enum (initial|change|refresh) — event family discriminator; default and dominant case is `change`. Named vocabulary: the `WSEnvelopeKind` enum in assets/schemas/enums.json
fields.topic: string — routing key the client subscribed to (broadcasts only; absent on command replies)
fields.type: string — discriminator naming the event family; matches the `name` field of the matching broadcast entry below
fields.ts: string — RFC3339Nano timestamp of the event; UTC
fields.payload: object — see the per-broadcast `payload` field for the schema reference

resume.description: Client → server: append `since: N` to a subscribe op to request replay of buffered events with seq > N matching the supplied topic patterns. Server → client: after the replay completes, the daemon sends one of two control frames. `{op:"replay_done", seq:N}` confirms the replay finished and carries the last-replayed seq (or the original `since` when the cursor is already at the top and nothing matched). `{op:"replay_lost", oldest_seq:M}` signals a gap the client cannot reconstruct — it must take a fresh GET /snapshot to resync and resume above `oldest_seq`. A gap arises in four situations: `since` precedes the oldest buffered event; `since` is above the daemon's current top, which is what a cursor from before a daemon restart looks like (the sequence counter is process-local and restarts at 0, and the envelope carries no epoch a client could compare); replay is disabled (`replay_buffer_capacity` 0), which can never satisfy a resume; or the connection fell behind and the daemon dropped queued events to keep it alive (one frame per overflow episode, not per dropped event). The replay buffer ceiling defaults to 1024 events; the per-connection outbound queue holds 1000.

heartbeat.description: The daemon sends a `{"op":"ping","echo":"<token>"}` frame every ping_interval_seconds. Clients MUST respond with `{"op":"pong"}` within read_timeout_seconds or the connection is closed. Clients behind NAT or mobile-data proxies that drop idle connections faster than read_timeout_seconds should additionally issue their own `{"op":"pong"}` frames pre-emptively — the daemon accepts unsolicited pongs.
heartbeat.echo: Opaque token on every server `ping`. A client that copies it verbatim into its `pong` (`{"op":"pong","echo":"<token>"}`) lets the daemon time the round-trip against its own clock alone; the two ends need no clock agreement. Echoing is OPTIONAL — a bare `{"op":"pong"}` is still a valid heartbeat, it just cannot be timed. Never parse the token; its encoding is not part of this contract.
heartbeat.rtt_ms: Round-trip time in milliseconds of the PREVIOUS heartbeat on this connection, carried on the next `ping`. Lets a client display its own latency to the daemon without measuring anything itself. Absent on the first ping and whenever the preceding pong carried no echo. This is the client→daemon distance only — it says nothing about the daemon→CCU path, which the `connection_latency_ms` hub metric reports separately.

reauth.description: Client → server: `{op:"reauth", token:"<bearer token>"}` swaps the credential behind an established connection without a reconnect. A socket resolves its identity once, at the upgrade, and the daemon closes it the instant that credential's deadline passes — so a long-lived client must refill before the deadline rather than discover the rotation through a 401. On success the daemon answers `{op:"reauth_ok"}`, carrying `expires_at` (RFC3339, UTC) when the new credential has a server-side deadline and omitting it when it has none. On failure — no token store wired, empty token, unknown or expired token — it answers `{op:"reauth_failed"}` and closes the connection; the client reconnects with fresh credentials. The same deadline is readable over REST as the `expires_at` field of GET /auth/me.
reauth.expires_at: string? — RFC3339 UTC instant at which the newly installed credential stops being accepted. Absent means no server-side expiry.

released_only.description: Client → server: append `released_only: true` to a subscribe op to drop every frame about a device the onboarding wizard has not released — the device.created / device.removed / device.availability_changed lifecycle frames and the datapoint.value_changed stream alike. Off by default and per connection, because this plane serves two kinds of consumer at once: the Config UI, which MUST see a device that is still being onboarded in order to configure it, and an ecosystem client, which must not adopt it before it is named. The `device.released` frame is never dropped — it is what lifts the filter, and withholding it would leave a filtering client unable to ever learn the device became adoptable. Frames that name no device (hub, system, alarm) are never affected. Pass `released_only: false` to turn it back off; an absent field leaves the current preference untouched across re-subscribes, exactly like `classify`.

subscription_ack.description: After a `{op:"subscribe", topics:[...]}` or `{op:"unsubscribe", topics:[...]}` is processed, the daemon echoes one `{op:"subscribed"|"unsubscribed", topics:[...]}` frame carrying the topics the client just requested. Reconnect-after-failure logic can use this ACK to confirm the subscription set survived the round trip without needing to inspect daemon-side state. An empty topics array suppresses the ACK to keep no-op subscribes quiet.

protocol_error.description: A text frame that is not valid JSON, or whose `op` is not one of the operations documented here, is answered with `{op:"error", error:{code:"bad_request", message:"..."}}` rather than being dropped silently. The connection stays open — only a WebSocket-framing violation (RFC 6455 §5, e.g. a binary frame or an interleaved fragment) closes it, with a close code instead of this frame.

command_schemas.description: Each command entry below may carry an `args` and a `result` field documenting its argument and return shape. `args` is an object whose keys are argument names; each value is a string of the form `<json-type>[?]` (with `?` marking optional fields). `result` follows the same conventions and may also be `"array"` or a fully-spelled object. Missing fields mean the command takes no arguments and/or returns an opaque object — the canonical source for the wire shape is then the matching Go handler under internal/north/rest/ws/.

optional_deployment_providers.description: Every command listed here is always present in `system.commands` and always dispatchable, but its domain provider is wired only when the deployment supplies it; when unwired, the command answers `{code:"not_implemented"}` instead of running. Check `system.commands` at runtime rather than assuming every catalogued command is functional in a given daemon build.

commands.description: Server-pushed: a CCU data-point change observable to a Custom-DP altered the CDP's aggregated state. SPA tiles subscribe to one CDP-scoped topic instead of N per-DP topics.
commands.name: custom_data_point.state_changed

commands.description: Server-pushed: the value of a wire data-point changed on the CCU. One topic per (device, channel, parameter) tuple. Subscribe with `classify:true` to receive inline category / data_point_type on the payload (default off). `value` is the raw CCU wire value; when the data point declares a non-trivial multiplier the payload also carries `display_value`, the same reading expressed in the unit the data point names. It matches the `display_value` on the REST data-point summary, so a client that seeds from REST and updates from here shows one consistent number. NOT filtered by onboarding release state: a device an operator has accepted but not yet released streams values here like any other, because the Config UI needs them to verify the device before releasing it. A consumer that adopts devices must therefore drop these frames for a device whose `released` is false — the state arrives on `device.created` and is lifted by `device.released`, both on the device's lifecycle topic. Filtering the device LIST alone is not enough.
commands.name: datapoint.value_changed

commands.description: Server-pushed: an optimistic write was rolled back (CCU never confirmed within TTL, or rejected it). Rides the same data_points topic as datapoint.value_changed — subscribers route by envelope `type`.
commands.name: datapoint.optimistic_rolled_back

commands.description: Server-pushed: a device's effective reachability flipped (its interface lost the connection, or the device itself reported UNREACH / STICKY_UNREACH). Rides the same device.{address}.lifecycle topic as device.created — subscribers route by envelope `type`.
commands.name: device.availability_changed

commands.description: Server-pushed: a device the daemon did not know before was observed in the registry. Not sent for the full-inventory announcement the CCU repeats after every reconnect — only an address the device registry does not already hold is announced, so a client may treat this frame as a genuine arrival rather than filtering the fleet out of it. The `source` field says which kind: NEW is a pairing, REFRESH a factory-reset re-pair (the device kept its address but rebuilt its channels), MANUAL an operator accepting a device out of the deferred-creation inbox, CACHE a device restored from the persisted description cache at boot.
commands.name: device.created

commands.description: Put a single device into pairing install-mode for a given duration.
commands.name: device.install_mode

commands.description: Server-pushed: an operator finished onboarding a device — it stops being withheld from the ecosystems (MQTT and therefore Home Assistant, the Matter bridge, outbound webhooks) and may now be adopted by a consumer of this API too. Rides the same device.{address}.lifecycle topic as device.created; subscribers route by envelope `type`. A broadcast rather than a reply, because the consumer that needs it is precisely the one that was already connected and filtered the device out on its device.created frame: without this push it would never learn the device became adoptable. NOTE: this API does not withhold an unreleased device — the Config UI has to see it to configure it — so a consumer that adopts devices filters on the `released` field of device.created and this frame lifts that filter.
commands.name: device.released

commands.description: Server-pushed: the CCU reported a device deletion. The same topic carries device.created — subscribers route by envelope `type`.
commands.name: device.removed

commands.description: Server-pushed: a non-state device event fired (keypress, impulse, device error) — one topic per (device, channel). Payload event_type / parameter disambiguate which trigger fired. Distinct from datapoint.value_changed.

commands.description: Write a paramset directly to the CCU without a session (non-transactional from a daemon-session perspective, but atomic on the wire: forwarded as one setParamsetValues XML-RPC call so the CCU applies all values together or none). Returns {written: N} on success. The CCU does not surface per-parameter status on this path — for that, use a config.session.* flow. MASTER and LINK writes are configuration changes gated behind the per-resource edit lock: pass edit_token (issued by POST /sessions/edit with key channel:{channel_address}:{paramset_key}) or the write is rejected with a 'locked' command error. VALUES writes are ungated.
commands.name: paramset.put

commands.description: Execute a CCU program by id. When `check_conditions` is true the CCU evaluates the program's "if" condition and runs the program only when it is satisfied; when false (the default) the program runs unconditionally. `executed` reports whether the program actually ran — always true for an unconditional run, false for a condition-checked run whose condition was not met. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one.
commands.name: programs.execute

commands.description: Delete a CCU program by id. Removes the program from the CCU (dom.DeleteObject) and drops it from the hub mirror. Admin-gated, mirroring the REST DELETE /programs/{id} route (deletion is irreversible). Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one.
commands.name: programs.delete

commands.description: List all CCU programs. Each entry carries optional `channel` / `device_address` fields when the program is associated with a device (device identifier in the program name); absent fields mean the entity belongs on the central hub card. `include_internal` overrides whether internal (Tmp_*) programs are listed; when omitted the central's include_internal_programs config default applies. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one.
commands.name: programs.list

commands.description: Start the diagnostic RPC session recorder across all centrals (clears prior data). Mirrors Python record_session (start).

commands.description: Report whether the diagnostic RPC session recorder is currently capturing.
commands.name: recording.status

commands.description: Stop the diagnostic RPC session recorder across all centrals. Mirrors Python record_session (stop).

commands.description: Acknowledge (clear) a single service message by id. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one.

commands.description: Acknowledge (clear) every quittable service message in one pass. The response carries the number acknowledged. commands.description: Kick a release check of the CCU add-on self-updater (ADR 0057). Fire-and-forget: progress and outcome arrive on addon_update.state_changed. Unregistered (unknown command) on platforms without the self-update capability.
commands.name: addon_update.check

commands.description: Start the verified download + firmware install of the latest CCU add-on release (ADR 0057). Fire-and-forget: the daemon restarts on success; failures surface on addon_update.state_changed. Unregistered on platforms without the self-update capability.

commands.description: Server-pushed: the add-on self-updater changed state (check finished, download/install progressing, failure). Only emitted on platforms where self-update is supported.
commands.name: addon_update.state_changed

commands.description: Server-pushed: the daemon is stopping. Emitted once during a graceful shutdown, before the servers stop, so a client can tell a stopping daemon apart from its own connection dropping — the distinction MQTT clients get from the broker's last will. A killed daemon cannot send it; detecting that stays the client's own job from its connection state.
commands.name: daemon_status.changed

commands.description: Force re-pull the CCU system-variable catalogue into the hub model. Optional central_name scopes the refresh to one CCU. Mirrors Python fetch_system_variables.

Each entry carries optional `channel` / `device_address` fields when the variable is associated with a device (explicit CCU channel assignment or a device identifier in the name); absent fields mean the entity belongs on the central hub card. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one.
commands.name: sysvars.list

commands.description: Update the value of a CCU system variable by name. Targets one CCU: `central_name` selects it, and may be omitted only when a single central is configured — with several the command is rejected rather than resolved against an arbitrary one.

commands.description: List the CCU programs that reference a system variable (native DPEnumUsagePrograms). Optional central_name disambiguates across CCUs.

commands.description: List all custom data points of all devices (or a single device when 'device' param is supplied).
commands.name: cdp.list

commands.description: Return a single custom data point by device address and name.
commands.name: cdp.get

commands.description: Invoke an operation on a custom data point (turn_on, set_temperature, open, …). Operation arguments use the units and scales a Home Assistant client expects, matching what the custom-data-point STATE reports — not the CCU wire values, which live on the data-point plane. Concretely for a colour light: set_color takes {hue, saturation} with hue in degrees 0..360 and saturation 0..100, the same scale `state.color.s` reports back; the daemon converts to the wire `SATURATION` fraction 0..1 itself. Read and write therefore need no conversion in either direction — scaling `state.color.s` before sending it back is the mistake this note exists to prevent.
commands.name: cdp.invoke

commands.description: List all calculated data points for all devices (or a single device / channel when params supplied).

commands.description: Return a single calculated data point by device address, channel number, and name.
